sections.h2: The fastest ways to sell in Haverstraw
sections.html:
Selling fastest in the Town of Haverstraw usually means a cash purchaser who takes the property as it stands. Listing with an agent or selling privately both depend on showings, financing and appraisals. If your house is in good order and nothing is pressing, a listing may still get you a better price.

The town sits in Rockland County along the Hudson River. It includes the Village of Haverstraw and hamlets such as Garnerville, Johnsontown, Ladentown, Mount Ivy and Samsondale. A seller deals with the town assessor, the town Receiver of Taxes, the town Building Department, and the Rockland County Clerk for the deed.

  • Agent listing: the usual path when the property is in good order.
  • Owner sale: keeps the fee, but you handle disclosure and contract work.
  • Cash sale: built for probate homes, houses needing work, or owners facing tax penalties.

Haverstraw had 40,462 residents in 2025, up from 39,087 in 2020, in 12,366 households averaging 3.11 people. Owners occupy 64.8% of homes, with a median value of $387,500. Median rent is $1,906, household income is $89,107 and the commute averages 30.1 minutes.

The town stretches from the Hudson River to the western county line across the northern part of Rockland County. The village of Haverstraw holds the historic downtown, and part of Harriman State Park, including Lake Sebago, Lake Welch and Lake Kanawauke, lies in the west. About a fifth of the town's area is water, so a lot beside the river or a lake should be checked for drainage and flood history before you set a price.

  • Roads: the Palisades Interstate Parkway, US 9W, US 202 and NY 45.
  • Ferry: the Haverstraw to Ossining crossing of the Hudson, tied to Metro-North.
  • Bus: Short Line buses run along US 9W into Manhattan.

Parcels in the Haverstraw-Stony Point Central School District, named on the town's tax collection notice, may pay school tax in installments. The first installment, at least half, is due by September 30. A second, at least half of what is left, follows in October, and the rest is due before early November. Your bill shows the district and the installment option, and buyers will want to see both.

Every parcel, vacant or built on, residential or commercial, gets a dollar value from the Town Assessor, and town, county and school tax all start from it. Exemption applications and STAR are handled in the same office, which also supports grievances, small claims assessment review and certiorari cases.

Haverstraw assessment calendar
DateAssessment step
July 1, prior yearValuation day
March 1Taxable status day
May 1Tentative roll filed
4th Tuesday in MayGrievance Day, heard by the Board of Assessment Review
July 1Final roll goes public

The filing window opens in May and shuts within a few weeks. Miss it and you wait for next year's tentative roll. The office provides a printable grievance application and a questionnaire for proposed assessments. Gather them before May.

January 1 through January 31 is the penalty-free period for town and county tax. Haverstraw, a town of the first class, adds 1% in February and 2% in March. On April 1, unpaid tax goes to Rockland County Finance.

  • Installments: bills above $50 may be paid in four parts, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31.
  • Later parts: due April 15, July 15 and October 15, and paid in Pomona to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance.
  • March payments: once March 15 passes, only bank or certified checks work, and they must be in the office when it closes on March 31. A postmark won't count.
  • Cards: taken, with a 2.45% convenience fee added by the card provider.

Owner-occupants who are elderly or disabled, in homes of up to three families, can ask the Receiver of Taxes to notify a third party using form RP-923. If you close partway through the year, have the closing attorney find out which installments are paid so the proration is right.

Building permits and Certificates of Occupancy come from the town Building Department, and section 84-4 of the Town Code spells out which repairs and construction require them. Those documents show that a house meets the codes for structural soundness and fire safety.

Look at every addition, finished basement and converted space before you list, and make sure a permit and a Certificate of Occupancy are on file for each. The department also takes questions about fire permits, burning permits, fire inspections and sprinkler systems. Expect a buyer's attorney to ask for a certificate on any addition or conversion. If a record is missing, raise it with the department early.

The Rockland County Clerk records Haverstraw deeds and wants originals that are recordable, legible, signed and notarized. New York charges $2 on each $500 of price, rounded up, which the seller normally pays.

The return and payment are due within 15 days of delivering the deed, and the clerk collects them when it records. On a residence of $1 million or more, the buyer owes an additional 1%. Downloadable forms for the common filings are posted on the clerk's land records page.

sections.h2: Selling a probate or inherited house
sections.html:
With an inherited house, every step raises the same question: who can sign. Before accepting an offer, collect the papers showing who may convey the property, because the deed must be signed and notarized in recordable form before it is filed. Also pull the latest town and county bill, the school installment record and any penalty notices, because unpaid tax keeps growing while an estate is settled. The Receiver of Taxes adds 1% in February and 2% in March, and on April 1 the balance moves to Rockland County Finance, so timing the sale around those dates can save money.

Estates often suit cash buyers, who accept the condition and work to the schedule probate allows. Still, have the buyer write down the closing date and who pays each cost.

sections.h2: Closing a cash sale in Haverstraw
sections.html: Cash deals take only a few steps. You accept an offer, attorneys exchange the contract, title is searched, and the deed is filed. A mortgage buyer would add an appraisal and a lender's calendar. Because the cash buyer takes the house as is, the open items are permits, tax installments and any lien, which must all be settled before title passes. Ask for proof of funds and a firm date on paper, and weigh the net against what listing would leave once commission and repairs are paid.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Haverstraw taxes after March?
faqs.a: Rockland County Finance takes over collection of unpaid bills on April 1. Until then the Receiver of Taxes adds 1% in February and 2% in March, and late-March checks must be certified or bank checks.

faqs.q: When can I grieve a Haverstraw assessment?
faqs.a: Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May every year, and filing starts May 1 and closes within weeks. In spring, call the Assessor's Office for the exact last day.

faqs.q: Can I pay Haverstraw taxes in installments if I am selling?
faqs.a: Yes, if the bill is over $50, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31. Later parts fall on April 15, July 15 and October 15, so ask your attorney which have been paid before closing.

faqs.q: Which authority records a Haverstraw deed?
faqs.a: That is the Rockland County Clerk, which takes only original documents that are legible, signed and notarized. File the transfer tax return within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: Will a buyer ask for a Certificate of Occupancy in Haverstraw?
faqs.a: They come from the town Building Department as proof a building meets code, and an attorney for the buyer may request one for an addition or conversion. Section 84-4 of the Town Code lists the work that needs permits.
